scanner_representation: Decode JSON objects as ordered raw key/value pair frames. Traverse child frames before their retained parent frame. A recurrence checkpoint stores the original fixed source, processed frame paths, emitted collision event ledger, and next frame path.

tested_crash_boundary.crash_point: Immediately after persisting frame path $ as processed and before appending the root collision event to the ledger.

tested_scope: Exactly one fixed-source deterministic local resume using the identical ordered raw-pair scanner and checkpoint representation from the predecessor result. The only changed crash ordering is that root frame path $ is durably marked processed before its already-discovered collision event is appended; no repair was tested.
observation: Because the checkpoint restored $ in processed_frame_paths while the root event was absent, the normal processed-path skip prevented any root rescan. The missing root collision event was therefore never reconstructed and was lost across recurrence.
scope_guard: This counterexample is limited to the demonstrated processed-mark-before-event-append root crash window, fixed source, collision-event semantics, and scanner/checkpoint representation. It does not establish failure for event-first ordering, transactional checkpoints, other event types, arbitrary Unicode classes, hostile-size behavior, or Phase-1 closure.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: after fresh authority freeze, own-state reconstruction, and required persisted/read-back preflight, test exactly one repair for this demonstrated inverse-order counterexample on the same fixed source and scanner representation: before allowing frame path $ to be persisted as processed, require every collision-event identity discovered for $ to already be present in the durable event ledger. Determine whether this precondition prevents the lost-root-event crash window; do not test a second repair in that invocation.
